facts.text: Oakland was chosen as the western terminal of the Transcontinental Railroad in 1869, making it a pivotal rail hub.
The city’s Lake Merritt became the United States’ first officially designated wildlife refuge in 1868, a National Historic Landmark today.
Oakland’s music scene birthed West Coast blues and jazz, and it still hosts artists across rhythm‑blues, funk, punk, and hip hop.
In 1966 the Black Panther Party was founded in Oakland, sparking a nationwide movement for Black power and civil rights.
General Motors opened its Oakland Assembly automobile factory in 1917, turning East Oakland into a major manufacturing center.
Lake Merritt, once a marsh, was dredged and surrounded by parks from the 1890s to the 1910s, creating the city’s iconic waterfront.
